newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - Colombian spreads ease.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - Colombian spreads ease.

text.p: Cash spreads on Colombian coffee softened this week despite signs of continued unrest in that country, while differentials on other grades held steady.
Processors were unfazed by reports Colombian leftist rebels had disrupted coffee shipments, noting that Colombian beans continued to find their way to the U.S. market.
"Colombia is shipping its quota of about one million (60-kg) bags a month," a trader said.
Indeed, signs of mounting trouble in the world's second biggest coffee growing country may have prompted exporters to step up the flow of shipments, he said.
"Everyone is trying to get coffee out as fast as possible because of the turmoil," he said.

Depending on the quality of the beans, spot Colombian MAMs into New York were offered anywhere from 18 to 22 cents over December "C" futures, down from a 24-25 cent premium a week ago. MAMs for October-November delivery, which had been moving steadily lower, held steady this week at 15 cents over "C".
But spreads on most other beans were little changed, as dealers focused on the scarcity of milds for spot shipment.
"There are really only Colombians and Brazils," one dealer said. "There are no Central Americans around."
